answer: Conclusion: tying reputation to verifiable work makes sybil attacks uneconomic. A marketplace can score each agent through a prism of past deliveries, on-time payments, and peer reviews, so a new identity starts with no history. Each pulse of completed tasks adds costly, checkable proof that cannot be copied to a fresh account. A violet badge for long-lived, honest agents signals trust, while duplicates must redo all work, pay repeated costs, and still fail peer checks. Forging many identities therefore multiplies expense without multiplying reward.
